title: Trend Following Is Changing Faster Than Ever - Systematic Investor - Ep.409

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Trend Following Is Changing Faster Than Ever - Systematic Investor - Ep.409.docx

speakers: Yoav Git (co-host, systematic CTA practitioner, caption 'Y of Git')
summary: July 2026 Systematic Investor: single-stock futures and compute-power futures, blow-up risk ranking of strategies, July 2026 counter-trend conditions, and a listener question on contract choice for commodity trend signals. Main segments: CFM 'Seven degrees of market structure' (0DTE retail option selling gives market makers positive gamma, causing intraday mean reversion, low index vol and record dispersion), the CFM short-term trend demise paper (volatility-normalised tick size; autocorrelation arithmetic), thematic factors, narrative momentum and equity trend diversification.

completeness_estimate: 0.85 - the first reader captured the CFM market-structure chain (0DTE gamma, dispersion, tick size), the commodity-contract answer and narrative momentum accurately; it missed secondary mechanisms and examples (maturity-specific ag risk, roll volatility adjustment, rational basis of underreaction, QIS human overlay, spread of short-dated options) and one unit mix-up.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: the tax implications or like various like uh uh practical implications of trading it.
claims.claim: Practical issues such as tax treatment of dividends and price changes for single-stock futures (and Kalshi compute contracts) can block adoption even when the instruments are attractive.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: the ability to short specific stocks will be useful.
claims.claim: Single-stock futures make shorting easy because no borrow is needed, giving CTAs and others new diversifying risk factors.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: being short a stock can be you know lethal because it's unlimited upside uh sorry unlimited downside if you're short
claims.claim: Retail access to shorting via futures is dangerous because short losses are unlimited (takeover risk).

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: CTA Minus futures came in as number 15 out of 17 uh with a green collar lower
claims.claim: A Sins Capital ranking placed managed-futures CTAs 15th of 17 on blow-up risk, vol-targeted diversified macro second lowest and short-vol/short-gamma the worst.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: anybody who manages their risk so CTAs and volatilitydriven macros
claims.claim: CTAs and vol-driven macro are defensive with upside bias in a blow-up, but not instantly protected, unlike short volatility which is dangerous.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: IBM lost 69 billion of market value in one day and that's about 25%
claims.claim: IBM fell about 25% in a day (from 332 to 213 in six weeks), showing single-stock gap risk.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: these chips don't last forever, you know. I mean, in the in the in the boom and bust you mentioned 2001
claims.claim: AI capex goes to chips lasting 2-3 years, unlike 2001 fibre which served for 20-25 years, so if AI fails recovery value is near zero.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: July is uh one another month of a little bit of adaptation
claims.claim: July 2026 saw geopolitical noise, ceasefire loss, oil reversal; managers split by speed on who was caught short energies.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: I think July has been counter trend um in general both you know in fixed income certainly and then FX
claims.claim: July 2026 was counter-trend in fixed income and FX (Japan bond and repatriation risk); dispersion in commodities by speed of trader.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: My trend barometer kind of reflects that it's it ended yesterday at 45.
claims.claim: Trend barometer at 45 is neutral.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: beta 50 down three basis points so pretty flat uh still up 8 and a half for the year.
claims.claim: As of 14 Jul 2026: BTOP50 +8.5% YTD, SG CTA ~+9%, SG Trend +8.76%, SG Short-Term Traders +4% (down 1.12% in July), MSCI World +11.15%, S&P 500 +11.32%, US Agg +0.41%.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG indices, MSCI World, S&P 500

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: in commodities you consume the commodity and then like it's a new commodity a month later or a few months later which which like the only thing which is connecting potentially different different months is storage
claims.claim: Commodity contract months are different assets linked only by storage/inventories, so risk factors differ by maturity (answer to listener question on modelling).
claims.testable: yes - compare contract-specific and front-contract signals

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: in the front contract of oil you will see a lot of CTAs, a lot of market makers, a lot of retailers
claims.claim: Front contracts are populated by speculators; deferred contracts by physical hedgers, so price dynamics move from short-term flows to long-term supply, demand and cost of production.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: let's capture 80% of the risk with just trading the front contract and it's very useful
claims.claim: Trading the front contract captures most risk, with lowest cost and highest liquidity; most of the industry uses the front contract history as signal.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: as you approach expiry the the volatility of the uh of the June contract that maybe have been less volatile a month ago suddenly goes to match the current front contract.
claims.claim: As a contract nears expiry its volatility converges to the front contract's, supporting use of front history; natural gas summer vs winter is an exception.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: in financial universe like 95 90 to 99% of the risk in commodities less so
claims.claim: The front contract explains 90-99% of risk in financial futures but less in commodities; trade deferred contracts only to capture different risk factors.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: if you're trying to calculate a carry in natural gas between the June and the December contract good luck to you
claims.claim: Roll yield and convenience yield in commodities must be contract-specific because seasonal contracts are unconnected, unlike trend signals.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: started flooding um started flooding the equity
claims.claim: CFM blog 'Seven Degrees of Market Structure': COVID-era retail inflows, API-based systematic retail, 0DTE options, rising dispersion and more mean reverting indices.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: a huge rise in the volumes of what's called zero day to expiry options in the index.
claims.claim: 0DTE index options exploded since weekly expiries in 2012, driven by retail selling at-the-money straddles to harvest the variance risk premium.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: It's an correlation is at an all-time uh low i.e idiosyncratic risk is at an all-time high.
claims.claim: Implied correlation/dispersion index shows single-stock variance far above index variance, globally at an all-time high.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: Um but over the last um the over the last 10 years buying the deep actually works much better.
claims.claim: Buying dips was historically a mistake but over the last 10 years the index has become more mean reverting and dip-buying pays within a month.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: retail has been selling options at the money near expiry. Okay, literally at expiry and that means that creates a very very strong positive gamma for the market makers
claims.claim: Retail selling of near-expiry ATM options gives market makers concentrated long gamma, whose delta hedging sells rallies and buys dips, creating an anti-trend flow every day.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: the autocorrelation of the intern like in intraday returns or one day returns in in equities have turned negative over time.
claims.claim: The 0DTE gamma effect reduces index realised and implied volatility and has turned intraday and one-day equity autocorrelation negative; single stocks are less affected.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: there's now more risk available there's in the uh in the single stock versus the the index than it ever has been because the index has been depressed in terms of the volatility.
claims.claim: Suppressed index volatility makes single-stock futures a better source of diversified risk for trend followers.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: I think what's driving the the single stock futures is more to do with the fact that retails want to short
claims.claim: Demand for single-stock futures is mostly retail wanting to short expensive AI valuations, with limited effect on CTAs.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: the volatility adjusted tick size is basically the size of the tick divided by the volatility of the underlying price.
claims.claim: Volatility-adjusted tick size = tick divided by volatility; as the S&P rose from about 1000 (1995) to 7000 the equity vol-adjusted tick shrank, unlike bond futures which stay near 100.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: the nature of the players that have entered the market and they are very much playing the anti-trend uh position
claims.claim: The blog gives a mechanism (retail 0DTE selling) complementing the CFM order-book sparsity explanation of why short-term equity trend has declined.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: a 16 basis point sharp negative 16 basis point sharp on your on your uh on your performance right
claims.claim: A 1% fall in one-day autocorrelation costs a 1-day-signal trend follower about 0.16 Sharpe, but a 5/20-day crossover only about 3bp per market (about 6bp across equities), so a 3% fall costs about 0.2 Sharpe for fast traders and little for slower ones.

correction.issue: Unit inconsistency: Git's 'basis points of Sharpe' mean hundredths of a Sharpe ratio (16bp = 0.16, 3bp = 0.03, 6bp = 0.06, about 20bp = 0.2). The first-reader text mixes '0.16 Sharpe' with '3bp' and '6bp', which reads as 0.0003 and 0.0006 Sharpe.
correction.fix: A 1% fall in one-day autocorrelation costs a trader using yesterday's price about 0.16 Sharpe (1% times about 16, the square root of roughly 256 trading days), but a 5/20-day crossover with roughly one-fifth weight on the one-day effect loses only about 0.03 Sharpe per market, or about 0.06 across a lightly diversified equity portfolio; a 3% fall therefore costs about 0.2 Sharpe for short-term traders and much less for slower (two-month) trend followers.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: trends are driven really by macroeconomic events more than just the order book structure.
claims.claim: Slower trend followers (2-month horizon) are insulated from intraday microstructure; alpha comes from long-term trends and macro events.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: markets that generally traded sort of higher at the open in the old days
claims.claim: Toby Crabel observed that open-to-close follow-through fell from about 58% to about 53-54%, a significant headwind for short-term managers.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: in the good old days uh the index might have explained 35%. These days it might be explaining 30 or 25%
claims.claim: Index explains a shrinking share of single-stock variance (35% to 25-30%); industry plus Barra factors take it to about 50%; themes (news-driven, transient) explain about 5% more, leaving about 45% idiosyncratic.
claims.indicator: variance decomposition: index, industry, factors, themes

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: actually sometimes these do not actually capture the volatility.
claims.claim: Thematic ETFs and bank QIS baskets are mostly exposed to industry, country or standard factors and fail to give pure theme exposure; build pure theme baskets yourself.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: it's less about prediction. It's really about risk about trying to identify where is the risk coming from
claims.claim: Decide how much extra risk single-stock futures, further contracts or themes add before trying to predict returns.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: there is the underreaction like it takes time for uh for investors and we are very familiar with that.
claims.claim: Narrative momentum (Satka et al., 13.3m articles, 2012-2023): slow-evolving themes show underreaction over about 6 months, and trend-following the news (stock beta to narrative) earns money distinct from price momentum.
claims.direction: long stocks with rising narrative exposure

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: to understand what the beta or the correlation between uh a certain stock and a narrative. It's a much more difficult exercise
claims.claim: Estimating stock-to-narrative beta is noisy when only about 5% of volatility is narrative-driven, so basket construction has large estimation error.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: with the rise of AI with the rise of our ability to harvest text and news
claims.claim: AI and machine learning now process news instantly, so the news underreaction/narrative momentum edge is likely to disappear quickly.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's actually being generated for each of us individually.
claims.claim: Agentic AI personalises news, so narrative truth becomes individual and may bias trading.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: equity index futures uh that we understand now covers about 30% of the equity risk that is available to harvest.
claims.claim: Equity index futures cover only about 30% of harvestable equity risk; medium and long-term equity trend remains fine.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: you don't want to double count right because you right. So like at the moment trading the semiconductors and the SMB you are basically trading the same thing.
claims.claim: Equity trend diversification layers: index, industry (avoid double counting, e.g. semiconductors vs S&P), Barra-style factors, narrative; construction and normalisation are hard, but the result can be nearly uncorrelated to index trend.
claims.indicator: index, sector, factor and theme trend components
claims.direction: build diversified equity trend with sector, factor and theme components

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: Kali is announcing uh forward curves for uh compute power for the cost of comput power. So that's a like a different uh a different type of uh of commodity which we've never seen before
claims.claim: Forward curves on the cost of AI compute power (priced off Nvidia chips) are a new commodity-like risk factor with no historical precedent, which a systematic manager can view as a diversifying exposure if its tax and operational treatment becomes clear.
claims.conditions: needs clear tax status and adequate liquidity
claims.testable: no - no price history exists yet

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there is definitely a little bit of a debate among um CTA practitioners um for sure and I don't know that that many of our colleagues have embraced them.
claims.claim: Adoption of single-stock futures among CTAs is mixed: a minority strongly favour trading single names rather than only indices, while most CTAs still stick to index futures.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if you were long only NASDAQ in 2001ish um you would have been down 85% at some point
claims.claim: Long-only equity exposure is not low blow-up risk: a long-only Nasdaq position fell about 85% in the 2000-2002 bust, so a low blow-up ranking for long-only equity is questionable.

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: As you go to further out on the curve, suddenly you're moving to the new crop. You really don't know what is going to be the supply.
claims.claim: In agricultural curves the front is driven by demand because the crop size is already largely known, while deferred contracts (new crop) are driven by supply risks such as weather and disease, so different maturities carry distinct risk factors and different diversification value.
claims.conditions: applies to crops with a harvest cycle (cotton, wheat)
claims.testable: yes - return correlation between front and deferred contracts

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: natural gas is an example um you know for example we would calculate the volatility on a specific contract or we would make the adjustment to when you roll the position in order to manage the risk slightly better
claims.claim: Where adjacent contracts differ materially in volatility (natural gas summer versus winter), a trend manager can compute volatility for the specific contract or adjust position size at the roll, so risk stays constant across the roll; for most markets using the rolled front series is still valid and there is no single correct answer.
claims.conditions: natural gas and other seasonal contracts
claims.testable: yes - compare realised portfolio volatility with and without roll adjustment

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: I think that mechanism that causes it is more the options.
claims.claim: Launching single-stock futures should not reduce single-stock dispersion because the cause is the index options explosion (0DTE), not the ease of shorting; single-stock options are less liquid and the CME contracts cover only about 50 very liquid names.
claims.testable: partly - monitor dispersion after the single-stock futures launch

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: we've seen a little bit in like in bond futures we've seen that um so we've seen again moving to weekly options at different days expiry um a little bit in oil and stuff like that.
claims.claim: Short-dated and weekly option expiries are spreading from equity indices to bond futures and oil, so the options-gamma mechanism that suppresses equity index trends could appear in other markets, with implications for short-term trend following there.
claims.indicator: weekly option volumes in bond futures and oil
claims.conditions: if option volume in those markets concentrates at-the-money near expiry
claims.testable: yes - test autocorrelation changes as short-dated option volume grows

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: they look at within each asset class what is the variation. uh the picture there is actually a lot more nuanced I would say
claims.claim: The CFM tick-size result is driven mainly by cross-asset differences (equities now have a much smaller volatility-adjusted tick than bonds); within each asset class the relationship is more nuanced, so the equity index finding should not be generalised to every market.
claims.indicator: volatility-adjusted tick size by asset class

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: we have seen maybe a drop of 3% in autocorrelation in the equity market over over the last 20 years.
claims.claim: One-day autocorrelation in equity returns has fallen by about three percentage points over roughly 20 years, enough to cost fast equity trend followers about 0.2 Sharpe while leaving slower, macro-driven trend followers largely unaffected.
claims.testable: yes - rolling autocorrelation of index returns

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: in the absence of complete information in the market, the fact that the price has gone up or the fact that other people are talking about a theme actually makes you evaluate your own valuation
claims.claim: Narrative underreaction has a rational explanation: with incomplete information, investors infer value from price moves and from what others discuss, so slow-moving themes diffuse gradually; fast, obvious themes such as war are priced instantly and show no lag.
claims.conditions: slow-evolving themes only; instant for obvious shocks such as war
claims.testable: yes - test underreaction by theme speed

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: I actually like the way that they do an uh a human overlay of the basket for the themes that they're doing.
claims.claim: Because statistical stock-to-narrative betas are noisy, one bank's QIS theme baskets add a human overlay (for example judging that Coca-Cola benefits from the World Cup even if it is not visible in price), which is sensible economically but non-quantitative and hard for a systematic manager to trade.
claims.testable: partly - human-curated basket construction cannot be replicated systematically

claims.speaker: Yoav Git
claims.quote: you're not just catching up to trend you're also catching up to the risk factor which is trading right now.
claims.claim: Narrative-based equity trend is harder than the other layers because the narrative covers only about 5% of variance and its identity keeps changing, so a manager has to track both the trend and which risk factor is currently live.
claims.testable: partly - requires a point-in-time news dataset
